1: IDEA: tangent_successor_residual
2: TITLE: Transition-directed tangent residuals preserve predictable coarse prefixes
3: MOTIVATION: The first generated token must be predictable from a user's recent item while later tokens retain item-specific distinctions; the available training transitions can supervise the residual direction without making the first level high-branching.
4: NOVELTY: Unlike cohort-anchor placement, behavior-conditioned curvature routing, or a behavior gate on first-level distance, this applies a directed transition signal to the *residual update between levels*: successor evidence bends the residual along a curved geodesic, rather than moving first-level anchors or adding a separate transition loss. T1 has 32 groups; T2/T3 retain most discrimination and T4 is collision extension only.
5: CHANGE: At each training item, use the train-only distribution of its observed successors to form a tangent-space direction at its selected T1 codeword, and subtract a bounded geodesic step in that direction before T2/T3 quantization. This changes the actual residual presented to subsequent quantizers; without transitions the step is zero, and with Euclidean geometry the parallel transport/log-exp construction is replaced by ordinary vector residual subtraction.
6: SPECIFICATION: Freeze train transition counts n_ij and p(j|i)=(n_ij+alpha)/(sum_j n_ij+alpha |S_i|) over observed successors S_i. Let m_i be the normalized weighted mean of frozen Stage1 embeddings of successors j (weights p(j|i)); for T1 anchor a_k and item latent x_i in the Poincare ball of curvature -c, form v_i=Log_{a_k}(Exp_0(m_i)) in T_{a_k}B_c, clip its norm to R, and set r_i=PT_{a_k->0}(Log_{a_k}(x_i)-eta v_i). Quantize r_i at L2/L3 using the baseline residual quantizer; hard T1 uses the baseline 32-way curved assignment. Capacity budget: T1 ≤ log(32)=3.47 nats; T2/T3 jointly carry the discriminative information (target 8–10 nats); T4 target <0.1 nats and remains deterministic collision extension. Cost: one precomputed successor prototype per item, then per Stage2 item in the batch one Log, vector subtraction, parallel transport and Exp-equivalent residual operation, O(Bd) beyond baseline; at 24 steps this is 24*B such operations per epoch, versus 24*24556*d scalar-scale operations if all items are covered once (about 600k item-ops/epoch, 3000 epochs), typically <10% arithmetic overhead and no Stage3 cost.
7: COST: Precompute train successor means in O(E_train*d), store one d-vector and count per item. Per minibatch add O(Bd) tangent/log/transport work (about 24*24556 item-vectors per epoch at full coverage; 3000 epochs), expected <10% Stage2 wall-time overhead subject to manifold-kernel cost; no added Stage3 cost.
8: HYPOTHESIS: Successor direction is predictable enough from a target item's training transition context that a small geodesic residual correction makes T2/T3 continuations easier to predict from the user's prefix, while T1 stays low-branching. Keep only if depth-1 survival does not fall, depth-2/3 survival rises, T4 NLL remains near constant and frozen Stage3 test_R@10 exceeds 0.065.
9: RISKS: Item-level successor averages can be multimodal and popularity dominated; a single direction may erase useful semantic residuals or leak source/target identity through a shortcut. If an item has few or no successors the estimate is noisy, and tangent transport may add instability.
